Theorem
[Variational and Euler--Lagrange solvability] 1. ch11:11.9\group gt-ch11 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0301 If $I$ is regular and $F$ is jointly convex in $(z,p)$, problem $\mathcal P$ has at most one solution. Its solvability is equivalent to solvability in $C^{0,1}(\overline\Omega )$ of (11.20) with boundary value $\varphi $.
Proof

\sketch A minimizer has zero first variation, hence solves (11.19). Conversely, if $u$ solves (11.19), convexity makes $t\mapsto I(u+t(v-u))$ convex with derivative zero at $t=0$, so $I(u)\leq I(v)$. Strict convexity in the gradient and the comparison principle give uniqueness.

□

For $K>0$, put \[ \mathcal C_K=\{ u\in \mathcal C:\| u\| _{C^{0,1}(\Omega )}\leq K\} . \] Problem $\mathcal P_K$ minimizes $I$ over $\mathcal C_K$; its minimizers are called $K$-quasisolutions of $\mathcal P$.
